name: Secure AI Quality Inspector
summary: An industrial automated fabric defect inspection and anomaly detection platform combining YOLOv8m, PatchCore, Grad-CAM, AES-256-GCM encryption, and 3-node federated learning.
recruiterExplanation: This project showcases Cimil's capability at the intersection of Computer Vision, Edge AI, Industrial IoT, and Distributed Systems. Built on real-world industrial datasets, the system handles supervised defect classification, unsupervised anomaly detection for never-before-seen defects, explainable AI with Grad-CAM, and privacy-preserving federated model updates across simulated factories—demonstrating production-grade ML engineering.
technicalExplanation: The architecture ingests camera images through an AES-256-GCM encrypted transport channel with SHA-256 integrity verification. Preprocessing applies CLAHE contrast optimization and bilateral denoising. A dual-model vision pipeline executes in parallel: a fine-tuned YOLOv8m model classifies known defects across 4 verified categories, while a PatchCore memory-bank model detects novel zero-shot structural anomalies. Predictions are visually explained with Grad-CAM activation heatmaps. The system computes severity metrics and estimated scrap cost in Indian Rupees (₹). A 3-node federated learning simulation using FedAvg trains models collaboratively across simulated factory nodes without centralizing raw fabric imagery.
architectureExplanation: Edge-to-cloud industrial inspection architecture. Client edge cameras transmit encrypted frames to a FastAPI backend. Inference outputs are served to a Streamlit operations console and stored in an encrypted database. Model updates are federated via decentralized weights aggregation.
features: PatchCore Unsupervised Anomaly Detection for Zero-Day Defects
Real-Time Defect Severity & Financial Loss Impact Scoring (₹)

faqs.a: YOLOv8 excels at rapidly localizing and classifying known, labeled defect classes. However, in manufacturing, novel or unseen defects can occur. PatchCore uses a memory bank of normal visual features to flag any abnormal deviations without needing prior training examples of that specific defect.

faqs.q: How does the federated learning component work?
faqs.a: A 3-node FedAvg architecture trains local models on private factory image batches, sending only gradient updates to a coordinator node that aggregates weights, preserving proprietary factory imagery and maintaining privacy.
